subject: Request: onshore enclave access + audit window — exec signoff for concession
messages:
From: Natalie Carawan <natalie@carawan.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — onshore enclave + audit

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the walkthrough today. To move forward with our pilot we need a few non-standard guarantees in the commercial and SOW layer:

- Onshore enclave: all processing for our tenant must run in an onshore VPC (US-East) that Carawan personnel can request scheduled, read-only log exports from. We do NOT need root or live shell access; exports only.
- Forensics snapshot retention: keep 60 days of immutable, time-stamped snapshots of request/response metadata (no raw customer data), with the option to extend to 90 days subject to exec approval.
- Audit window: Carawan needs a 30-day rolling audit window and a one-week notice for scheduled audits.
- Security docs: we will need SOC2 evidence and a short runbook describing how exports are generated.
- Commercial: we are targeting a 36-month commitment with an aggressive ARR ramp. To justify the contract and the additional operational constraints, procurement is requesting a 25% committed-volume discount and a one-time onboarding credit.

I attached Carawan's SOC2 and the compliance checklist. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate the enclave/export model and the snapshot retention? If this requires an executive exception, please escalate — procurement needs an answer by Friday so they can align internal stakeholders.

Best,
Natalie
CTO, Carawan Innovations

Attachments: carawan-soc2.pdf (summary), procurement-checklist.xlsx (referenced)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Private deployment questions — onshore enclave + audit

Marissa / Jordan — forwarding Carawan's asks. Quick summary and my read:

- Technical: Onshore VPC hosting in us-east + read-only scheduled exports of audited logs = feasible with Redwood Private. We cannot provide live shell access or on-demand SQL access; exports must be served by platform tooling.
- Retention: platform can do 60-day immutable snapshots today; 90 days is not standard — requires exec OK and potential cost uplift.
- Audit mechanics: 30-day rolling window + one-week notice is fine; full on-site forensics not permitted (platform-managed exports only).
- Commercial: customer wants 25% off for 36 months + onboarding credit. My recommendation: signoff up to 18% committed discount + cover onboarding credits up to $30k; anything beyond needs exec approval.

Attached SOW draft with the enclave/export language highlighted. Please advise next steps — Jordan, can you run pricing impact and escalate to Markus if needed? Procurement asked for an answer by 2026-10-16 EOD.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW-draft-Carawan-v1.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Carawan enclave terms + discount request (RDW-57321)

Marissa / Markus —

I've reviewed Logan's recommendation and run preliminary pricing. Key points:

- Infrastructure delta: reserving an onshore enclave (size: 2 dedicated nodes with isolation policies) will add an estimated $18k/mo cost at list.
- Operational overhead: scheduled export tooling + compliance packaging estimated one-time $22k.
- Revenue profile: 36-month commit is attractive; ARR ramps to ~$1.1M year 1.

Given both the infra delta and the business upside, I propose we allow a one-time exception:
- Approve up to 18% committed discount (netting the reserved infra cost)
- Approve 60-day immutable snapshot retention as the default (not 90)
- Audit access limited to scheduled read-only exports; no live host access
- Require legal to include an indemnity carve for forensic misuse + additional SLA credit (1% service credit) if any maintenance window impacts customer access to the enclave

If Markus can greenlight this as an exec concession we can close by next week. If we want to meet the customer's full ask (90 days / 25% discount) that will need a senior commercial waiver with a defined economics memo.

Attaching the security brief for reference.

Thanks,
Jordan
Deal Desk — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-security-brief.pdf

On Wed, 14 Oct 2026 at 11:03, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Carawan enclave terms + discount request (RDW-57321)

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the clear economics and the risk mitigations. I approve the exception with the following conditions:

1) Commercial: authorize an 18% committed-volume discount for the 36-month term and a one-time onboarding credit not exceeding $30k. Any additional discount beyond this threshold requires VP Sales approval and a margin impact memo.

2) Retention & audit: allow 60-day immutable snapshots; deny the standard 90-day ask. Audit access will be via scheduled, redwood-generated exports to a mutually agreed S3 bucket or secure transfer — no live host or console access.

3) Operational guardrails: require a Runbook addendum in the SOW that details export frequency, data fields included (metadata-only for snapshots), and escalation steps. Require 30 days notice for any data-retention changes.

4) Legal & Compliance: Legal must add an indemnity clause limiting liability for exported data and a clause that ties SLA credits to operational impact. Compliance must sign off on the export mechanism and the SOC2 evidence we provide.

5) Timebox: This approval is a one-time, customer-specific concession and will be valid for the closure of this deal only. Any future requests for longer retention or broader access require a new escalation.

Logan — proceed to update the SOW to reflect the approved language and get Legal's markups into DocuSign. Jordan — coordinate the final economics in HubSpot (RDW-57321). Marissa / Karthik — confirm the infra provisioning timeline and whether we need any additional CAPEX approval.

-Markus
SVP, Sales — Redwood Inference
